key_insight: Flex4DHuman turns a single or sparse set of views of a moving person into synchronized dense multi-view video, using only relative camera pose information. The key breakthrough is that it removes the need for explicit geometry priors like skeletons, depth, normals, or target-view rendering.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing dynamic 4D humans from limited input views, especially when accurate geometric priors are unavailable or hard to obtain. It aims to generate consistent, dense multi-view observations of a subject over time.
method: Uses a multi-view video diffusion model to generate synchronized dense multi-view videos from monocular or sparse multi-view inputs.
Conditions generation with relative camera-pose positional encoding instead of skeletons, depth maps, normals, or rendered geometry.
Learns view-consistent temporal and spatial dynamics directly from data, enabling flexible 4D human reconstruction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a simpler and more flexible route to 4D human reconstruction by reducing dependence on hand-crafted priors and preprocessing. It can improve robustness in real-world settings where camera setup is sparse and geometric cues are incomplete.

paper_title: Flex4DHuman: Flexible Multi-view Video Diffusion for 4D Human Reconstruction
paper_authors: Jen-Hao Cheng, Yipeng Wang, Hao Zhang, Gengshan Yang, Jenq-Neng Hwang
